showcase.note: Interval and the order analysis ask each other at assignments and prove checks neither proves alone; every kind of inline annotation appears once.

showcase.title: Widening, then narrowing
showcase.note: Nested loops: the inner head widens j to [0,+inf] and narrows it back, so the outer counter is proved non-negative.

showcase.title: Dead code from a sign
showcase.note: Goblint's tutorial in the Sign domain: a guard infeasible on a negative value leaves its whole arm unreachable.

showcase.title: Recursion, computed exactly
showcase.note: Entry-state contexts evaluate mutual recursion value by value, and refute a wrong annotation carried over from Goblint.

showcase.title: Call strings keep callers apart
showcase.note: At depth 2, two activations of a shared callee no longer merge, so both results stay exact.

showcase.title: Widening per origin
showcase.note: The FM 2026 paper's update rule: widening each call site's contribution separately recovers the precise bounds.

showcase.title: Flow-insensitive globals
showcase.note: The FM 2026 paper's Fig. 1 with g and h each at its own unknown: g's writes join to [-17,42], enough for g < 43 but not g == 42, and h widens to [0,+inf]. Set Program globals to Flow-sensitive and every check is proved.

showcase.title: A reduced product
showcase.note: Int combines Interval's bounds with Congruence's residue to pin a remainder no component decides alone.

fixtures.name: straight line refuted
fixtures.summary: Mirror of 01-straight_line_proved.vimp's PROVED witness: an exact negative write refutes the same condition instead of proving it. Pairs PROVED and REFUTED witnesses for one mechanism (exact assignment), rather than leaving REFUTED coverage to a single case buried inside a mixed-verdict file.

fixtures.name: unknown after random
fixtures.summary: Unconstrained value from __voblint_nondet_int(): nothing bounds x before the check.

fixtures.name: no exclusion set
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/01-cpa/28-interval.c (x != 0 in the true arm of if (x)) and 36-apron/18-branch2.c. Inside if (x) and if (!!x) every execution has x != 0, so the concrete result is fixed. Goblint proves it through DefExc's exclusion set {0}. No component of the reduced product Sign x Interval x Parity x Congruence can represent "everything except 0": the sign lattice has no NonZero element (its non-trivial elements are Neg, NonPos, Zero, NonNeg, Pos), an interval is convex, parity and congruence cannot carve a single point out of Top. The guard refines x to Top in every component and (x != 0) stays UNKNOWN. interval and sign alone answer the same.

fixtures.name: nonrelational join
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/01-cpa/28-interval.c (a != b is UNKNOWN there too). Every execution leaves (a, b) at (8, 9) or (9, 8), so a != b concretely holds. The join after the branch is pointwise: a and b each become [8,9] and the state no longer records that a = 8 pairs with b = 9. An interval domain has no way to relate two variables, so (a != b) over [8,9] x [8,9] is UNKNOWN. int agrees.

fixtures.name: interval plus inverse is identity
fixtures.summary: On the true arm of x + 1 < 5, every execution has x <= 3, so x < 4 holds. Interval's inverse of < refines x + 1 to [-inf,4], but its inverse of + is the identity, so nothing reaches x and the check stays unknown. An interval analysis that inverts addition, x := x meet (r - 1), would prove it (Nipkow and Klein, Concrete Semantics, Sect. 13.8.3).

fixtures.name: disjunction judged in one state
fixtures.summary: Inside the guard x is 1 or 2, so x == 1 || x == 2 holds in every store. check_query (Abstract_Checks.thy) judges both disjuncts in the same state x=[1,2]: eq([1,2],[1,1]) and eq([1,2],[2,2]) are both unknown, and so is their disjunction. The disjunction is never re-judged under the refinement of its first operand. Goblint's CIL front end lowers || into branches, so there the second operand is judged after the first has failed. The nested form below does not help Voblint either: inv_eq_ivl (Interval_Backward.thy) leaves both intervals unchanged on a definite inequality, so the else branch of x == 1 keeps x=[1,2] instead of [2,2].

fixtures.name: conjunct order
fixtures.summary: Both guards state 0 < i < j < 10, so i <= 8 and j >= 2 hold in both arms. bfilter (Backward_Domain.thy) refines a conjunction from right to left (bfilter (And b1 b2) True d = bfilter b1 True (bfilter b2 True d)), each conjunct once, without iterating to a local fixpoint. Which bound reaches which variable therefore depends on the order of the conjuncts: in the first arm i=[1,8] but j=[-inf,9], in the second j=[2,9] but i=[1,+inf]. Repeating the pass would give i=[1,8] and j=[2,9] in both.

fixtures.name: if else
fixtures.summary: Branch and join: y is 1 or 2 depending on the arm taken, so the check holds on every path regardless of which arm the analysis takes.

fixtures.name: while loop
fixtures.summary: Counted loop: exercises widening/narrowing on a bounded induction variable.

fixtures.name: branch refinement after random
fixtures.summary: __voblint_nondet_int() gives x no bound at all (Top), but the guard on each branch narrows it before the check runs: the true arm's assume tightens x to [1,+inf), the false arm's to (-inf,0]. Both checks read back their own arm's narrowed range, not the pre-branch Top -- a guard/assume-narrowing regression, not a join regression (unlike 01-if_else.vimp, the check is inside each arm, before any post-if join). The false arm's (x <= 0) is a permanent regression witness for interval_less_false's boundary fix (Interval_Numeric_Queries.thy): it used to report UNKNOWN here because interval_less_false required a STRICT upper<lower separation (u2 < l1) to refute "0<x", missing the touching-boundary case x=[-inf,0] where u2=l1=0 -- sound but needlessly conservative, now u2<=l1.

fixtures.name: infeasible disjunct dropped
fixtures.summary: "0 < y" holds on the then-branch: x is 5, so the second disjunct "(x < 0) == 1" is false in every state, and the branch is taken only when the first disjunct is true.

fixtures.name: infeasible conjunct dropped
fixtures.summary: The conjunctive half of the branch gate, dual to 04-infeasible_disjunct_dropped.vimp. Concretely "y < 1" holds on the else-branch: x is 5, so "(x < 0) == 0" is true in every state, and the branch is taken only when the second conjunct is false.

fixtures.name: interval sanity battery
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/01-cpa/28-interval.c, the interval sanity battery, without its UNKNOWN checks: the true arm of if (x) and the a/b correlation live in known-imprecision/01-no_exclusion_set.vimp and known-imprecision/02-nonrelational_join.vimp, the nondet-decided a == 8 and b == 8 in soundness/01-truthiness_guard_underdetermined.vimp. What stays: truthiness guards (if (!x), !!t, !f, dead arms of if (a) and if (!a)), constants joined into [8,9] and every <, <=, >, >= threshold on them, comparisons as int values, a counted loop with x == 10 after it, and the tail after Goblint's early return restructured as nesting because main may not return. int gives the same verdicts.

fixtures.name: truthiness guard refinement
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/36-apron/18-branch2.c and 27-inv_invariants/03-ints-not.c. A bare int as a condition means != 0, so the true arms of if (!i) and if (!x) both refine the nondeterministic value to exactly [0,0]: i == 0 and x == 0 are PROVED and i < 0 is REFUTED (Goblint: bare, bare, FAIL). The other arms only learn "not 0", which decides nothing about i >= 1 or x == 1; those UNKNOWNs are in soundness/01-truthiness_guard_underdetermined.vimp. sign and int agree.

fixtures.name: disjunct arm pollution interval fixed
fixtures.summary: x == 0 && x == 1 is self-contradictory (no integer is both), and so is y == 0 && y == 1; either disjunct's own two-step backward narrowing intersects x's (or y's) interval down to Bottom. bfilter_lifted (Backward_Domain.thy) canonicalizes each arm to structural Bottom before joining, so the pointwise And/Or join no longer lets the other disjunct's untouched x (or y) location survive and override the narrowed-Bottom arm: the whole guard comes back witness-bottom, and the branch is recognized as unreachable.

fixtures.name: if without else
fixtures.summary: A false branch leaves x unchanged and reaches the following statement. A true branch executes its body and reaches the same continuation.

fixtures.name: else if chain
fixtures.summary: Exactly one arm executes; a chain may omit or include its final else.

fixtures.name: bounded loop guard refines body
fixtures.summary: x = 0; while (x < 20) x = x + 1. The loop head settles at x = [0,20] without widening loss: the guard x < 20 narrows the body entry to [0,19], the increment gives [1,20], and its join with the initial [0,0] is the head value again. The exit is [20,20]. The EXPECT-GRAPH block pins the head, body and exit values and the compiled CFG layout (pp1 loop head, pp2 body entry, pp3 exit).

fixtures.name: direct comparison guards both polarities
fixtures.summary: Backward guard refinement of x = [0,20] against the threshold 10, for each direct comparison and both branch polarities, plus x < 20 and a guard no state in y = [5,9] satisfies, whose arm is dead. x != 10 leaves x = [0,20] on its true arm (an interval cannot exclude an interior point, see known-imprecision/01-no_exclusion_set.vimp) and narrows it to [10,10] on its false arm.

fixtures.name: truthiness guard underdetermined
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/36-apron/18-branch2.c (i >= 1 is UNKNOWN!), 27-inv_invariants/03-ints-not.c (x == 1 is UNKNOWN!) and 01-cpa/28-interval.c (a == 8, b == 8 are UNKNOWN). Each value is an unconstrained __voblint_nondet_int(): inside if (i) the guard only rules out 0, so i = 1 and i = -1 are both executions; likewise x inside if (!!x). a and b are 8 or 9 depending on the nondet z. Every check has a satisfying and a violating run, so UNKNOWN is the only sound verdict -- refining if (i) to [1,+inf] would be a soundness bug, and this fixture is the witness against it.

fixtures.name: proc layout recursion
fixtures.summary: Procedure layout regression: the procedure list is known before any body is compiled, so a call may target the current procedure (f's direct self-recursion), a sibling declared later (g calling h, a forward reference needing no second pass), or a mutually recursive pair (g and h calling each other). The claim here is purely structural -- which callee each call edge targets, and where each procedure's block starts and ends -- not a value the analysis proves. G defaults to 0 and neither branch of f's body changes it, so f's own condition G<1 holds at every recursive re-entry: f provably never reaches its else branch, never returns to main, and the trailing check after inc() is therefore proved dead (NOWARN) -- a true consequence of the source. The graph below marks that check [dead] at pp13, agreeing with the DEAD the text report prints for it: both readings come from the same solved table, so a check the analysis proves unreachable cannot read as decided in one and dead in the other. The graph snapshot below pins which callee each call edge targets and each procedure's block layout; the call and combine edges after f's call site still appear in it; only their solved state is dead.

fixtures.name: two call sites same procedure
fixtures.summary: Two call sites to the same procedure share ONE activation context (--graph-snapshot shows both "enter square(...)" edges landing on the same cluster_ctx_1): square's entry is one CFG node, revisited once per call site, not resolved per call site. This is call-site (in)sensitivity -- a context-sensitivity gap distinct from (and not fixed by) the Base-style D/G migration that resolved 04-globals/precision/ 02-global_var.vimp's flow-insensitive global summary: even with the whole abstract state lifted into the local unknown, the entry node itself is still keyed on the unit context, so the D/G solver evaluates it once against both incoming edges. Under the warrowing update rule this repeated evaluation widens the entered parameter's bound on the second visit, so neither call's own exact argument (9 or 16) survives -- both checks come back UNKNOWN, not a narrower sound join. A call-string- or entry-state-context-sensitive analysis keys the entry per call site or per entered value instead (see precision/04-two_call_sites_entry_state.vimp).

fixtures.name: two call sites join solver
fixtures.summary: x == 6 and y == 20 hold concretely, but without a context both calls share twice's single FunctionEntry unknown. Its seed receives p = 3 from one site and p = 10 from the other; the join rule joins them to [3,10] without widening, so the one analyzed body returns [6,20] to both callers. The bounds survive (contrast the warrow default in 19-paper-examples/known-imprecision/04-context_insensitive_calls.vimp, which widens to [6,+inf]); the per-call values do not.

fixtures.name: call return
fixtures.summary: Procedure call with a formal and a used return value.

fixtures.name: caller local survives call
fixtures.summary: A call with no relation to x (not passed as an actual, no shared global) must leave the caller's own binding of x untouched across the call -- the D/G combine step at the call-to-return edge restores the caller's locals rather than merging in anything from the callee's activation.

fixtures.name: callee local does not leak
fixtures.summary: bump's local x (its formal's shadow) and main's local x are distinct activation-local bindings that happen to share a name. If combine ever let a callee's local leak back into the caller's own binding of the same name, main's x would come back as 105 instead of surviving at 1 -- this is the same activation-local boundary #99's D/G combine fix protects, exercised through a name COLLISION rather than an unrelated call.

fixtures.name: two call sites entry state
fixtures.summary: Same program as known-imprecision/01-two_call_sites_same_procedure.vimp, under entry-state context sensitivity instead of the default flat analysis. There, both calls to square share ONE activation, whose entry is widened across the two call sites (n = [3,+inf]), so a and b read back [-inf,+inf] and neither can be proved. Here, each call is keyed by its own entered argument value ([9,9] vs [16,16] respectively), so square is analyzed once per distinct entry-state context instead of joined into one shared summary -- an observable precision benefit of #108's context analysis over the flat default, not a different claim about the concrete program (both checks are true for the same reason in both files: 3*3=9, 4*4=16).

fixtures.name: dead branch no bottom leak
fixtures.summary: Minimal reproducer from issue #113: n=5 makes "n < 2" false, so the "return 1" branch is provably unreachable. Before the reachability-lift fix, the dead branch's own #ret := 1 assignment transfer still produced a non-bottom #ret=[1,1] from an already-unreachable predecessor state, and the exit node's join widened the result to a=[1,500] instead of the exact a=[500,500]. Locks in the fixed, precise result -- flat, no procedure recursion, no --context flag. The recursive-factorial variant of this same pattern is 06-recursive_factorial_dead_branch_no_bottom_leak.vimp, which proves its results exactly under entry-state context sensitivity.

fixtures.name: recursive factorial dead branch no bottom leak
fixtures.summary: Recursive factorial under entry-state context sensitivity. Solver-key inspection (not just this CLI report) confirms context separation itself is exact: factorial's entry is covered by four distinct, precise contexts (n=[1,1], [2,2], [3,3], [4,4]), each with an exact n.

fixtures.name: two call sites entry state join solver
fixtures.summary: Same program as 04-two_call_sites_entry_state.vimp, explicit --globals join instead of entry-state's implicit Warrow default. The routed entry-state equation system names no solve function of its own -- only the shared D/G spec and the routing policy -- so it is exactly as solver-independent as the flat Ctx_None equation system already is, and this program crosses no loop under either context, so join needs no widening to terminate and reproduces the exact per-context result.

fixtures.name: two call sites entry state per origin solver
fixtures.summary: Same program as 04-two_call_sites_entry_state.vimp, explicit --globals per-origin instead of entry-state's implicit Warrow default -- see 07-two_call_sites_entry_state_join_solver.vimp for why the routed equation system underneath accepts any solver the same way the flat one does.

fixtures.name: two call sites share resume node
fixtures.summary: Both branches of the if end in a call to the same procedure, so both calls resume at the same CFG node: the compiler emits pp4 --call-to-return f--> pp6 and pp5 --call-to-return f--> pp6. That node's equation therefore carries two call actions to f, both routing to the same context, so one right-hand-side evaluation performs two side effects to the same callee-entry seed key.

fixtures.name: two live call sites share resume node
fixtures.summary: The sibling of 09 with no dead branch: an unconstrained condition leaves both call sites reachable, and they enter f with different values, so the two side effects to the shared callee-entry seed key carry two genuinely different states rather than bottom and a state.

fixtures.name: shared resume node per origin solver
fixtures.summary: 09's program under an explicit --globals per-origin. The shared resume node makes one right-hand-side evaluation write the callee-entry seed key twice, and per-origin is the update rule that shape is sharpest against: it keeps one slot per write origin and overwrites that slot, so a partial accumulate replaces a completed one from the same origin rather than joining into it.

fixtures.name: shared resume node join solver
fixtures.summary: 09's program under --globals join, which folds every contribution into one slot and therefore never dips: this case terminates with or without the per-key aggregation. It is here as the control. Aggregating writes changes when a key is published within one right-hand side, so it changes the order the solver visits unknowns in, and narrowing is order-sensitive -- a mode that was already healthy is exactly where an ordering-induced precision regression would show up unexplained.

fixtures.name: shared resume node distinct callees
fixtures.summary: Two call sites sharing one resume node, but to different procedures, so the node's two call actions carry two distinct seed keys rather than one key twice. Aggregation must keep them apart: a per-key accumulator that collapsed distinct keys would publish f's entered state into g's seed and vice versa, which is unsound rather than merely imprecise.

fixtures.name: shared resume node entry state context
fixtures.summary: 09's program under entry-state context sensitivity. Both call sites enter f with the same argument, so formals_context derives the same context for both and the two routed seeds land on the same key -- the collision survives context sensitivity precisely when the two calls agree on the entered formals, which is the case a per-call-site keying would otherwise be assumed to separate.

fixtures.name: shared resume node in loop
fixtures.summary: The shared resume node inside a loop, so the seed key is written twice per right-hand-side evaluation and that evaluation is itself revisited under widening and narrowing. Aggregating the two writes moves the key's publication to after every contribution has been read, which reorders the unknowns the solver visits on the first pass; narrowing is sensitive to that order, so a loop is where a reordering that costs precision would surface.

fixtures.name: entry state random arg
fixtures.summary: Acceptance case for #108's entry-state context analysis: an unconstrained argument (__voblint_nondet_int()) must collapse to ONE wide entry-state context at p's call site -- the entered value's own abstract state, not a context keyed per concrete value -- so the analysis terminates instead of diverging over every value __voblint_nondet_int() could produce. The checked condition inside p is itself unconstrained by that wide context, so UNKNOWN is the only sound verdict here; the acceptance claim is that entry-state context sensitivity runs and reports soundly for an unbounded argument, not that it proves anything about this particular check (see precision/04-two_call_sites_entry_state.vimp for the precision benefit entry-state context sensitivity actually buys on a bounded argument).

fixtures.name: repeated call site widening
fixtures.summary: The concrete value of total here is fixed at 7, so total < 100 genuinely holds -- but the analysis cannot establish it. Mechanism: the loss is on total, not on the entered formal. inc's body writes total := total + n, so total's own value re-enters its next contribution and the chain 0, [0,3], [0,7], ... ascends without bound; Apinis warrowing must cut the upper bound to +inf to terminate. The following narrowing phase recovers the lower bound (total is [3,+inf], not [-inf,+inf]) but not the upper one, so a bound like < 100 stays undecided. n itself is exact at [3,4].

fixtures.name: counter widened by call
fixtures.summary: counter is called twice from the same call site, so its concrete value at the check is fixed at 2 -- yet the analysis cannot bound it above. Mechanism: a declared global's write inside a called procedure feeds the shared unknown's own equation (the assignment reads the same slot it writes), so the two contributions ascend ([0,0], then a self-referencing [0,1], [0,2], ...) and warrowing must widen the upper bound to +inf to terminate -- the same call-site widening as 04-globals/known-imprecision/01-repeated_call_site_widening.vimp. A single call to p, by contrast, needs no fixpoint iteration and resolves counter exactly; it is the repetition, not the declaration itself, that costs precision here. Contrast with 04-globals/precision/05-glocal_not_global_by_name.vimp: same program, same two calls, but Glocal is undeclared and stays exact throughout.

fixtures.name: shared global joins writes
fixtures.summary: The sequence of 06-sequential_global_proved.vimp with program globals flow-insensitive. x lives at its own global unknown, which must cover every value x holds anywhere: the initial zero, published by the program entry, joins the two writes, and the check at the end sees x in [0,1]. The exact check is lost; the range check survives.

fixtures.name: global default zero
fixtures.summary: A declared global's value before any write is its documented Goblint-style zero-initialized default (cinit_sign_st), read back exactly -- see also 02-global_var.vimp (Interval), which locks in a declared global's value after it is actually written.

fixtures.name: global var
fixtures.summary: Declared global mutated across two calls; exercises declared_global_vars wiring. Base-style migration acceptance case (issue tracked alongside 12-widening/precision/01-global_self_feedback.vimp): total lives in the same reachability-lifted local unknown as every local, flow-sensitively through both calls to inc, so its exact value (7) survives to the check -- no separate flow-insensitive global summary exists to join total's prior value against its own write anymore.

fixtures.name: global across calls entry state
fixtures.summary: Call/return semantics of the entry-state context analysis over a declared global. The local unknown carries every VIMP variable, so g crosses the call boundary in the same slot a local does: bump reads the g main wrote before the call, writes it, and returns it, and main then observes both the returned value and the callee's update. The three calls carry different arguments -- two literals and one that is itself the global g -- so bump is analyzed under three distinct entry-state contexts ([5,5], [4,4], [19,19]) and n binds exactly in each. The third call also locks in that a global-valued actual argument is evaluated against the caller's real state at the call site, not a globals-bottomed one.

fixtures.name: global written constant
fixtures.summary: A declared global written with a constant, then read at a check in the same procedure -- no call, no self-reference. Distinct from 01-global_default_zero.vimp (a global read before any write, at its zero-initialized default) and from 12-widening/precision/01-global_self_feedback .vimp (a write that reads the global's own prior value): this is the plain case that has neither, and it pins that having a global at all costs no precision.

fixtures.name: glocal not global by name
fixtures.summary: Glocal is spelled like a global-naming convention but is never declared global, so declared_global_vars excludes it: it is an ordinary local, routed flow-sensitively through every call like any other local, and its exact value survives untouched no matter how many times p is called. Declaration -- never spelling -- decides globality; see 02-counter_widened_by_call.vimp for the properly declared global counter in this same program, which the repeated call widens.

fixtures.name: sequential global proved
fixtures.summary: x := 0; x := 1; check(x == 1) with x a declared global and no call in between. The current pipeline proves the check: within one procedure a declared global lives in the same reachability-lifted local unknown as every local (see 02-global_var.vimp), so the second write's exact value reaches the check with no flow-insensitive join against the first -- there is no separate shared-slot summary here for the two writes to join through. Contrast with 07-sequential_local_proved.vimp, the same sequence with x an ordinary local: both give the identical exact result, which is the point -- declaring x global costs nothing as long as no call crosses it.

fixtures.name: sequential local proved
fixtures.summary: The contrasting baseline for 06-sequential_global_proved.vimp: the same x := 0; x := 1; check(x == 1) sequence, but x is an ordinary local. Tracked flow-sensitively per program point, so the second write's exact value reaches the check with no join against the first -- identical result to the global version, since no call ever crosses x in either.

fixtures.name: callee writes global and undeclared local
fixtures.summary: Declaration, not spelling, decides storage class: p writes both the declared global counter and the undeclared Glocal. combine keeps the caller's locals and adopts the callee's globals, so main sees counter's write and not Glocal's. If Glocal were classified global, Glocal == 1 would be REFUTED. One call site, so counter's seed has one origin and needs no widening (contrast known-imprecision/02-counter_widened_by_call.vimp).

fixtures.name: global through two callees
fixtures.summary: Gx = 4; inc(); sqr(); with inc adding 1 to the declared global and sqr squaring it. The global is analyzed flow-sensitively through both calls (see 02-global_var.vimp), so (4 + 1) * (4 + 1) = 25 reaches the check exactly. The EXPECT-GRAPH block pins the compiled interprocedural CFG: inc at pp0-pp1, sqr at pp2-pp3, main from pp4, calls at pp5 and pp6.

fixtures.name: multiple checks
fixtures.summary: Several checks in one program with different expected verdicts: this pins that one report carries all three, not any single verdict.

fixtures.name: constant refuted
fixtures.summary: A constant-false check in reachable code is REFUTED, not NOWARN: unlike 06-reachability's check(false) sentinels, this location is not dead code, so the check actually executes and its condition is decidably false every time.

fixtures.name: same condition main first
fixtures.summary: Two checks with the same condition and opposite verdicts, with main written before the procedure it calls. The compiler lays out procedures before main, so the result lists f's check first while the source has main's first. Each report row carries its check's own source position as its label, so each verdict lands on its line; pairing rows with checks by order of occurrence would swap the two.

fixtures.name: guarded interval trio
fixtures.summary: Ported from Example_Interval_Checks_Store_Only.thy (checks_ivl_ex_classify_2/3/4, checks_ivl_ex_report_eval). fixtures.name: reachable
fixtures.summary: Mirrors Goblint's "__goblint_check(1); // reachable": a trivially-true condition isolates "does this location produce a report entry at all" (a CFG-compilation completeness property) from "is the analysis precise enough to prove this specific fact" -- 'true' is provable in every abstract state, live or dead, so its presence is the only thing being tested here. x is unconstrained (__voblint_nondet_int()), not a known exact value, so neither if-branch is infeasible -- both stay genuinely reachable, unlike an exact guard (see infeasible_guard_nowarn.vimp, where a known-exact x makes one branch provably dead).

fixtures.name: unreachable nowarn
fixtures.summary: Code after 'return' is unreachable: mirrors Goblint's "__goblint_check(0); // NOWARN (unreachable)". The dead check's report row carries DEAD in place of a verdict: the analysis proves the point unreachable and says so, where Goblint only stays silent, and never prints the vacuous PROVED a bottom state would otherwise satisfy. main itself may not contain a return (wf_source_program's no_return conjunct), so the return lives in a helper procedure p instead, called destination-less.

fixtures.name: infeasible guard nowarn
fixtures.summary: A NOWARN case that is NOT return-based: x is narrowed to [5,5], so the "if (x < 0)" branch is infeasible. bfilter correctly detects this and narrows x to an empty (but non-canonical) interval there, e.g. Ivl (Fin 5) (Fin (-1)) -- not the canonical Ivl PlusInf MinInf bot. This case is why is_bottom_ivl compares bounds directly rather than testing "<= bot": a "<= bot" test would miss this branch's emptiness entirely (it only matches the one canonical representative), silently leaving a dead check visible with a vacuous PROVED verdict.

fixtures.name: unreachable after return literal
fixtures.summary: Literal Goblint idiom (https://goblint.readthedocs.io/en/latest/developer-guide/testing/): "__goblint_check(0); // NOWARN (unreachable)" -- a constant-false check as a dead-code sentinel, rather than a real condition that happens to be dead (see 02-unreachable_nowarn.vimp for that variant). VIMP has no integer truthiness, so the literal constant is the bexp "false" itself. main itself may not contain a return (wf_source_program's no_return conjunct), so the return lives in a helper procedure p instead, called destination-less.

fixtures.name: unreachable dead branch literal

fixtures.name: forward feasibility branch gate
fixtures.summary: The branch transfer's forward feasibility gate, not backward narrowing, is what makes this branch dead. Backward narrowing alone cannot: bfilter's Eq case inverts "(x < 0) == 1" to an empty target for its left operand, but afilter has no narrowing rule for a comparison node, so the empty target is dropped and the incoming state survives unchanged. The gate instead evaluates the whole condition forward -- interval_tobool of [0,0] answers Some False -- and contradicts the selected polarity, so the then-branch has no successor at all and its check is reported DEAD.

fixtures.name: infinite loop exit dead
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/00-sanity/05-inf_loop.c and 03-practical/09-nonterm2.c. The loop body is reachable, so its check(false) is REFUTED (Goblint: FAIL!). The loop's exit edge is the guard's negation, !(true), and the branch gate evaluates it to Some False in every state: nothing after the loop has a successor, so both trailing checks are reported DEAD (Goblint: NOWARN (unreachable), formerly NONTERM). The second trailing check reads x so the DEAD row is seen to hold for a check over a bound variable, not only for the literal sentinel.

fixtures.name: nested infinite loops
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/03-practical/22-nested-infinite-loops.c (issue #231), which only asks that the CFG survive; the checks here pin which points are live. The inner while (true) never exits, so the outer body's tail and everything after the outer loop are dead: their checks are reported DEAD. The check at the top of the outer body runs on every entry of the outer loop, and since the outer loop's back edge is itself dead, x is still exactly 0 there -- the head sees only its entry state.

fixtures.name: strict loop enter
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/00-sanity/26-strict-loop-enter.c. Goblint's note is that the node after Pos(x>50) ends up dead while the diverging inner loop keeps its widened x = [51,2147483647]; here the TD solver re-evaluates the branch's dependents on narrowing, so the inner loop head, its body and the check after it all end at bot and the check is reported DEAD (Goblint: NOWARN (unreachable)). fixtures.name: disjunct arm pollution fixed

fixtures.name: nondet guard recovers nonneg

fixtures.name: counting loop nonrelational join
fixtures.summary: Adapted from Goblint tests/regression/36-apron/94-simple-apron-interval.c (Mine's counting loop, HOSC 2006); Goblint's interval configuration marks all three UNKNOWN as well. Concretely N >= 0 after the clamp, X counts from 0 up to N and stops exactly at X = N, so X == N and X - N == 0 hold in every execution; the else arm of if (X == N) is never taken and N == 8 holds too. The loop head joins X = [0,0] with the widened body state and keeps X and N as independent intervals [0,+inf]: the fact X = N is a relation between two variables and no non-relational domain retains it, so the loop exit's (X >= N) only bounds each side. Both equality arms then look live, N becomes [8,42], and N == 8 is UNKNOWN for the same reason. An octagon or a polyhedron would recover X = N; int agrees with interval.

// Truncation toward zero and dividend-signed remainders differ from floor
// division for negative inputs. Zero-divisor results are VIMP conventions.
fun main() {
  __voblint_check(7 / 3 == 2); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-7 / 3 == -2); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(7 / -3 == -2); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-7 / -3 == 2); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(7 % 3 == 1); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-7 % 3 == -1); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(7 % -3 == 1); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-7 % -3 == -1); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-7 / 3 * 3 + -7 % 3 == -7); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(2 / 3 == 0); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-2 / 3 == 0); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(7 / 0 == 0); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(-7 % 0 == -7); // PROVED
  __voblint_check(20 / 3 % 4 * 2 + 1 == 5); // PROVED

  __voblint_check(0 && 1 / 0); // REFUTED
  __voblint_check(1 || 1 % 0); // PROVED
}

fixtures.name: parity cannot bound value
fixtures.summary: The boundary of what Parity can say, kept as an explicit witness so the PROVED cases next door are not mistaken for general-purpose precision. x is Even here and the concrete value is genuinely fixed (4), but the parity lattice has exactly four elements -- Bot, Even, Odd, Top -- and carries no magnitude information whatsoever, so "x is Even" is the most it can conclude and x == 4 stays UNKNOWN. The concrete mechanism: parity_classify_check decides an equality only when the two sides' parities are disjoint (Even vs Odd), which refutes; it can never confirm one, since equal parity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for equal values. --analysis interval proves this same check outright.

fixtures.name: even odd distinct
fixtures.summary: The acceptance case for Parity as a public analysis: a property provable from parity information alone. n is completely unconstrained, so no interval or sign reasoning bounds x or y at all -- but times_parity has PEven * _ = PEven, so 2*n is Even whatever n is, and 2*n+1 is then Odd. Even and Odd are disjoint, so x and y can never be equal; parity refutes the equality and therefore proves its negation. Multiplication by the literal 2 is what makes this non-relational: the domain evaluates each operand independently, so n+n would be Top+Top=Top (it cannot see the two operands are the same value), while 2*n is Even from the literal's own parity alone. This exercises the full public path: run_voblint answers --analysis parity from the routed-unit solved result -- the same generic pipeline the other domains use, with no Parity-specific result or report construction anywhere in it.

fixtures.name: parity across call
fixtures.summary: Parity through a procedure call and return, so the routed spine's own enter and combine edges carry the fact rather than just intra-procedural transfer. double's return is Even for any argument (PEven * _ = PEven), and the caller reads that back across the combine edge, so b+1 is Odd while a is Even and the two can never be equal -- provable at the call site even though the original argument is unconstrained. Context-insensitive (the default --context none): one shared callee context suffices here, since both calls agree on the callee's parity result.

fixtures.name: contradictory equalities dead

Parity's equality inverse gives both sides of a guard that held the meet of their parities: x == 1 makes x odd, then x == 0 meets odd with even and leaves Bottom. The y arm empties the same way, the lifted filter canonicalizes each empty arm to Bottom before the join, and the branch is proved dead.

Goblint recurses through main itself; VIMP's main cannot be called, so the recursion lives in a helper. rec decrements the global num_iterat from 11 and recurses while it is positive, then returns 5 from the num_iterat == 0 base case, and every level passes 5 back up. The result is proved in every mode, including --context none: the base case's num_iterat == 0 guard selects the `return 5` arm on any state containing 0, and the recursive arm only forwards that value.
